solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Our neighbour pours energy into Stalinist factory

parts.note: a Stalinist is a communist, a Red

indicators.note: pours, with into, says one piece is poured inside another
into, after pours, gives where the energy letter goes: inside the factory word

parts.note: a factory is a plant
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Industrial propaganda: a Soviet factory driven to pour ever more energy into production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our neighbour' sounds like the people next door, but it is the planet beside Earth. 'pours ... into' is a single instruction split around the energy letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars, called the red planet, is the next planet out from Earth, so it is our neighbour in the solar system.

clue.text: Playing-field program cut short, not to cover any new ground

definitions.text: not to cover any new ground

parts.note: REC is short for recreation ground, a British public playing field

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the program word is lopped off

parts.note: an app is a program for a phone or computer

explanation.surface: A sports-ground software project is curtailed before it breaks any new ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last P from APP. A rec (recreation ground) is a British town's public playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise is to go over points already made, so it covers no new ground.

clue.text: Contribute fully, though showing no inclination?

definitions.meaning: to try as hard as possible, giving one's all
read literally, being at one's most level is showing no slope at all; the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.surface: Someone gives their all to a cause even though they seemed reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like willingness, but it is a slope: a thing at its most level has none.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to try one's hardest, which is contributing fully to a task.

clue.text: Sadly mistaken, start to cheer title

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters of Sadly are got wrong, rearranged

parts.note: hip is how the cheer hip hip hooray starts

explanation.surface: Someone sadly mistaken begins to cheer a title they thought they had won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges SADLY to LADYS; HIP opens the cheer 'hip hip hooray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Her Ladyship is a form of address for a titled woman, so the word is itself a title.

clue.text: Common sense is all but pointless

indicators.note: all but means everything except the last letter of the pointless phrase

parts.note: pointless means of no use, written as NO USE

explanation.surface: A grumble that ordinary good sense is almost completely futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops the last letter of NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is a British informal word for practical intelligence, i.e. sound judgement.

clue.text: Speak irreverently of capture to no purpose

parts.note: to capture is to take
done to no purpose is done in vain

explanation.surface: Mocking a capture as pointless, as if speaking lightly of a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the commandment against using God's name lightly, i.e. speaking of something without due respect.

clue.text: Heavens returning that a hymn covers

indicators.note: returning means the hidden run is read backwards
covers means the words that a hymn contain the run within them

explanation.surface: A churchgoer notes heavenly matters returning as a theme a hymn covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' hides TAHYM in 'that a hymn'; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated exclamations of surprise, used like 'goodness me!'.

clue.text: Revolutionary teacher upset native islanders

parts.note: Mao Zedong led China's communist revolution

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for teacher is turned upside down

parts.note: Sir is what British pupils call a male teacher

explanation.surface: A radical teacher has upset the people native to some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIR up the column to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: In play, chuck earth over series of pots on top of building

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the first piece sits above the next
on top of in a down clue puts the pots piece above the building
to chuck is to throw about, so the letters of earth are tossed into a new order

parts.note: in snooker a break is a run of successive pots
a house is a building

explanation.surface: A potter chucks clay over a row of pots stacked on a building, all in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chuck' rearranges EARTH to HEART; a snooker break is a run of pots.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a George Bernard Shaw drama of 1919, so it is a stage work.

clue.text: New orders out for house badge

indicators.note: new means the letters of orders out are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Fresh instructions go out to replace a school house's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges ORDERS OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The red and white rose was the heraldic emblem of the royal House of Tudor.

clue.text: Noisy bird kept by family died — utopia!

indicators.note: kept by means the noisy bird is held inside the family word

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
noisy means loud
a cuckoo is a bird
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A noisy bird kept as a family pet dies, and someone exclaims sarcastically about paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' holds the noisy bird within the family word, with the death letter tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Aristophanes' Birds, means an unrealistic ideal world, a fantasy perfect place.

clue.text: Asleep at work? I ask you

indicators.note: at work means the letters of Asleep are busy being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone caught sleeping on the job, and an exasperated 'I ask you!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges ASLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the polite word used in making a request, as when one asks a favour.

clue.text: Ominous as no end of wine is knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means the whole run is read backwards, as a drink is knocked back
no end of means the wine word loses its last letter

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: A boozer's grim omen: there is no end to the wine being knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' and 'knocked back' both read as drinking talk; the reversal covers both the trimmed wine and 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinister suggests evil to come, as an ominous sign does.

clue.text: Be on the street picking up slippers, not even parking inside

indicators.note: inside means the parking letter is placed within the rest
picking up in a down clue means the slippers word is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: eels are slippery creatures, so slippers in a cryptic sense
a surface that is not even is rough
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A homeless person picks up a pair of slippers on the uneven pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippers' looks like footwear but means slippery fish; 'picking up' reads that word upwards in this down clue, and 'inside' slots the parking letter in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping without a bed, outdoors, is what someone living on the street does.

clue.text: Lose one's senses and prepare to parade with nothing on

parts.note: soldiers fall in, taking their places in line, before a parade
love is a score of nothing in tennis

explanation.surface: A soldier, made to parade naked, nearly loses their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smitten is traditionally a kind of madness in which reason departs.

clue.text: Strong censure one received, like Abednego

indicators.note: received means the numeral is taken in by the other pieces

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for strong or loud
a reproof is a censure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A biblical figure receives a stern dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' puts I after F and before REPROOF. Abednego, with Shadrach and Meshach, walked unharmed out of Nebuchadnezzar's furnace in the Book of Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abednego came through a fiery furnace untouched, so he was resistant to flames.

clue.text: Opening of bottles: port and spirit

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Opening bottles of port and spirits at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like a drink to go with the port, but it means verve.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and liveliness, the same as spirit in the sense of vivacity.

clue.text: Astonishing events as drivers get through long distances

indicators.note: get through means the drivers piece goes inside the distances word

parts.note: miles are long distances
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Drivers cover huge distances, which is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' is not people at the wheel but their club: the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation offering roadside rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonders that seem to defy nature are supernatural, astonishing happenings.

clue.text: To wander in small wood not good

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: Wandering in a little wood is not a good idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from GROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam aimlessly is to wander, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Wish Joy to pull out, in the outcome

indicators.note: in means the drawing-out word goes inside the outcome word

parts.note: fate is the outcome, what eventually happens
to elicit is to draw out, pull out

explanation.surface: Someone named Joy is wished well, but pulls out, waiting on the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy' looks like a woman's name, capitalised only to mislead; it is plain happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to wish them happiness.

clue.text: Ruined abbey site is a bit close

parts.note: a whit is a tiny bit
by means close, nearby

explanation.surface: A ruined abbey is a bit too close for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitby is a North Yorkshire seaside town with a famous ruined abbey on its cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: The town's clifftop abbey ruins are its best-known landmark, so the abbey's site.

clue.text: Seafood cut back severely

indicators.note: back means the cutting word is read backwards

parts.note: to clip is to cut
severely, as in hit hard

explanation.surface: Seafood is cut back hard, as on a severe menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CLIP into PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: This small oily fish of the herring family is eaten as seafood, often tinned.

clue.text: Turning round front of tap, place to dry out washer

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembly is turned backwards
round means the clinic word goes around the letter from the tap

parts.note: rehab is a clinic where addicts dry out

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A plumber turns a tap and leaves a washer somewhere to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washer' looks like a tap part but is someone washing. 'round' puts T inside REHAB to give REHTAB; 'Turning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bathing is washing themselves, so the word is a washer in a literal sense.

clue.text: Soundly erected, to be knocked down with spades not unknown

indicators.note: not, with with, means spades come in instead of the unknown
soundly means the word for erected is taken by how it is said

parts.note: something erected has been raised
Z is an algebraic unknown
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A building put up soundly is to be demolished, with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' turns RAISED into its sound-alike RAZED; 'with spades not unknown' puts S in place of Z.
explanation.definitionFit: This spelling is an old variant of raze, to demolish, so it means flattened.

clue.text: Mischievous child, not complete fraud

indicators.note: not complete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A naughty child is not wholly a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not complete' drops P from SCAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A con or swindle is a fraudulent scheme.

clue.text: Commonly, genuine regret distorts a person's proper allegiance

indicators.note: commonly means in common speech, where the opening aitch of the genuine word is dropped

parts.note: genuine means honest
rue is regret
to colour a view is to distort it

explanation.surface: Genuine regret commonly distorts a person's sense of where their loyalties lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' drops the H of HONEST, as Cockney speech does ('onest).
explanation.definitionFit: Colours are the flag one fights under, so showing one's real ones reveals genuine loyalty.

clue.text: Insect eats it, right?

definitions.note: an adjective, right, standing for an adverb, rightly: the question mark signals the stretch

indicators.note: eats means the insect word takes in the following word

parts.note: a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone asks if an insect is eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival in the clue but must be read as an adverb, 'in a right way'; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means suitably or properly, so in a fitting, right way.

clue.text: Some hated to destroy what settler built up

indicators.note: to destroy here means the letters of Some hated are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Some people hated destroying what a pioneer built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to destroy' rearranges SOME HATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer settling new land would build a farmhouse and holding: a farm estate.
